data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding opened at GBP 389.009m. Analysis of the claims development triangle shows adverse prior-year development of approximately GBP 71.205m (18.3% of opening gross reserves), indicating a net strengthening of reserves. Management attributes the deterioration primarily to an exceptionally active 2020 Atlantic hurricane season, US wildfires and several large casualty/political risk losses, with COVID-19-related exposures being reserved (GBP 15.6m net of reinsurance) but only producing limited notifications. The movement is therefore primarily driven by natural catastrophe and large man-made losses leading to adverse claims development across property and casualty portfolios.
raw_causal_phrases: The result was also notably influenced by the most active Atlantic hurricane season in recent memory

In addition to Covid-19, 2020 was the most active Atlantic hurricane season in recent memory combined with further Wildfires in the USA resulting in claims of $36,800k net of reinsurance to Syndicate 2468.
There was also significant risk loss activity, particularly in the Casualty and Political Risk classes.
the Covid-19 pandemic has also affected the result, where there have been a limited number of claim notifications.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Statement of Financial Position (Liabilities - Claims outstanding) prior-year column. No explicit textual single-line 'movement in prior years' gross figure found; prior-year development computed from the gross claims development triangle (gross, GBP 000). Exact reserve descriptive sentence for prior-year movement not present. Some named losses are described in USD ($36,800k) and have not been converted; COVID-19 reserve quantified net of reinsurance (GBP 15,600k) and reported as net. Segmental analysis includes direct insurance and a negative reinsurance acceptances line; percentages reflect values as printed and therefore include a negative reinsurance acceptances contribution.
